answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated escrowed exchanges with independently enrolled counterparties; a registry limits each verified person or organization to one sponsoring identity, and disputes can slash the sponsor’s bond. A sybil farm therefore needs scarce enrollment and locked capital, then must sustain costly, consistent trade to build trust. Like a canyon narrowing a stream, the bottleneck makes each fake identity expensive; copied claims are only an echo, not evidence, and nectar-like rewards arrive only after verified delivery.
